data.name: Valerian
data.gender_notes: Valerian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Valerian is derived from the Latin word valere, which means 'to be strong' or 'to be healthy'. In Christian tradition, it is the name of a number of saints and martyrs, including Saint Valerian of Rome, who is believed to have been a Roman soldier converted to Christianity by Saint Peter. The name Valerian carries the meaning “Strong, Healthy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Valerian usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, healthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and courage in faith.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Valerian total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Valerian I (253-260 AD): Known as 'the Perfect' or 'the Great', Valerian was a Roman Emperor who came to power through military means. He is most famous for his ill-fated campaign against the Sassanian Empire of Persia, which resulted in his capture and eventual death. This defeat marked a turning point for the Roman Empire, as the Sassanians were able to exploit Rome's vulnerability and gain significant territorial gains.

Valerian II (974-991 AD): Valerian II, also known as Valerian the Great, was a Holy Roman Emperor. He was the son of Otto I and succeeded him upon his father's death. Valerian is notable for his military campaigns against the Magyars and his role in the Investiture Controversy. The controversy centered on the relationship between the power of the secular ruler and that of the Church, specifically regarding the investiture of bishops and other church officials.
